experiment: FirstTrial v3 — stoppage handling and spell stability
scope: Exploratory scores on the same public five-minute sample used in v1 and v2; 7,500 graded frames and 17 possession spells.
design: Eleven fixed comparisons: three reference methods plus soft or forced tracking-supported stoppages, minimum-duration decoding, and set-piece support. No parameter search or automatic winner selection.

bootstrap.interpretation: 90% percentile range over the 17 public-example possession spells; not independent validation.

component_findings.duration_effect: The tested 0.32 s team and 0.40 s dead-state limits changed only 1–8 graded frames. No duration variant changed spell F1 or possession count.
component_findings.set_piece_support_effect: Raised soft-cost spell F1 from 0.297872 to 0.308333, but the result remained below the reference and v2 shape methods. It lowered the forced-label spell F1 from 0.285714 to 0.274510.
component_findings.interpretation: Dead-ball frame detection improved, while possession-spell agreement declined and predicted possession counts rose. The public sample is too small to pick a full-match winner.

limitations: The public sample has only 17 possessions and was already used in v1 and v2; it is not independent validation.
Automatic Smart Tagging set-piece intervals are approximate phase windows, not confirmed whistles or possession labels.
Collective stillness can mistake slow live play for a stoppage; hard D overrides can split true possession spells.
The duration decoder uses future observations and is an offline model, not a live real-time predictor.
No full-match answer labels are available; full-match accuracy and the best component mix remain unknown.
